brief.scope: Review only the four-document adoption interface completion against owner/adoption/producer inputs and accepted discovery/C1/C2/lane-policy contracts. Check concrete closed descriptor/request/decision/observation shapes, unambiguous safe forwarding and model selection, resume/MCP binding, correct refusal versus unreachable, canonical ownership and viable independent implementation. Verify examples/links within this read profile; static checks suffice where commands are unavailable. Preserve Daybreak dispositions and no activation/authority claims. Do not reopen accepted architecture or demand future code. No source/tests/settings/host writes, network or vendor launch. Inline REVIEW <=1400 words, actual model and exact ref, approve/changes, remaining actionable findings.

findings.claim: The frozen descriptor types launch_id as discovery's ID (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, discovery-lever.md:74), which cannot hold the canonical execution identity `<UTC stamp>-<stage>-<harness>-<6 hex>` (dispatch CONTRACT.md:469, e.g. 20260906T103421Z-code-codex-20aa14: uppercase, 34 bytes). The same section relies on "the existing execution record" for model observation (line 366) and on "Existing canonical records carry custody and receipts, no new store" (line 384), yet no descriptor field binds the descriptor to that record. Independent implementers must either invent a second identity namespace with an undeclared correlation or violate the declared type; either way the descriptor-to-record edge is undeclared under verified-couplings obligation 1.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '336p;366p;384p' ops/conductor/conductor-start-plan.md; sed -n '74p' ops/conductor/discovery-lever.md; sed -n '469p' ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md

findings.claim: harness-capabilities.md:209 ("SHA256, ID, Selection and digest encoding come from startup") and probes-lever.md:258 ("exact startup Selection") cite a named type `Selection` that the startup document never defines by that name: conductor-start-plan.md gives only an inline `selection` table row (line 338). The capitalized name is already taken in the same contract family by discovery-lever.md:490, `Selection = {selection:"none"|"one"|"multiple"|"unknown", ...}` for handoff selection, which is what lane_start returns. Two documents that must be built to independently now cite an ambiguous type.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '209p' ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md; sed -n '258p' ops/conductor/probes-lever.md; sed -n '338p' ops/conductor/conductor-start-plan.md; sed -n '490,492p' ops/conductor/discovery-lever.md

findings.claim: The change narrowed the Conventions sentence to "Every `probes.py` verb is a read" (line 21) so the new live section would not contradict it, but left the file's Exits section absolute: "2 (Rejection) — the refusal wire says why. Nothing here can Abort" (lines 150-153). The added section then declares "A supervision abort retains partial observations and exit 3" (line 294) in the same contract file. One contract now states both that nothing here can abort and that a documented arm exits 3.

"The descriptor's adapter fields must match this identity" (line 242) joins two differently-shaped closed objects with no declared mapping: descriptor adapter is `{revision,grammar_sha256,executable_sha256,config_sha256}` (conductor-start-plan.md:342) while identity adapter is `{revision,mechanism,config_sha256,grammar_sha256,normalizer_sha256}` (line 216). executable_sha256 has no identity.adapter counterpart (it lives under harness.executable.sha256, line 215), and mechanism/normalizer_sha256 have no descriptor counterpart. Consequently the descriptor digest that permission-surface.md binds every tool Request to (binding_sha256, line 96) does not cover the pinned normalizer, although the capability tuple is said to be "extended by grammar, tool-normalizer and MCP binding digests" (line 92).
findings.reproduce: sed -n '92p;215,216p;242p' ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md; sed -n '342p' ops/conductor/conductor-start-plan.md; sed -n '96p' ops/conductor/permission-surface.md

findings.claim: permission-surface.md freezes the policy-side entry point `evaluate_tool(bound_role, normalized_request)` and the closed Decision shape (lines 88, 139-146) while asserting "Policy lives once in lane-policy.md#bootstrap-and-minimum-complete-activation" (lines 78-79). lane-policy.md contains no occurrence of evaluate_tool; it declares only the module home ops/conductor/tools/lane_policy.py (line 417). The counterpart declaration belongs to adoption bucket 1a, which was outside this producer's four owned files, but nothing in the change records that the citation is still awaiting its counterparty, so it currently dangles.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '78,79p;88p;139,146p' ops/conductor/permission-surface.md; grep -c evaluate_tool ops/conductor/lane-policy.md; sed -n '417p' ops/conductor/lane-policy.md

findings.claim: The report's cleanup field admits three values, `complete`, `failed` or `unreachable` (line 263), but the exit mapping covers only two: "Report exit 0 requires every requested arm PASS, matching verified identities and cleanup complete. Exit 1 carries FAIL or UNREACHABLE rows or cleanup failure" (lines 290-291). An all-PASS run whose cleanup outcome could not be observed is barred from exit 0 and is not named by exit 1, leaving a declared state with no declared exit class in a document whose stated purpose is closed shapes.

The prose beneath the CLI synopsis was rewritten to govern "Tokens after the first `--`" (lines 85-87), but the synopsis block (lines 78-83) still shows four forms with no `--` position and no optional token group. Whether forwarding is admitted with the two `test` forms, and where `--` may appear relative to `<profile>`, is unstated, so the unit's own object — an unambiguous safe forwarding surface — is left open at the CLI boundary even though the grammar below it is closed. The pre-existing sentence had the same gap; this change edited the sentence without closing it.

The frozen Decision refusal example embeds the wire's own field separator inside a field: needed is "use canonical dispatch; run the independent doctor for gate diagnosis" (line 146), while docs/wire.md defines the serialized line as `class: expected <what>; found <what>; needed <remedy>` and the conformance gate asserts expected-found-needed on that line. A validator splitting the serialized refusal on "; " sees four segments for this fixed template. The startup example at conductor-start-plan.md:410-411 avoids this.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '146p' ops/conductor/permission-surface.md; sed -n '408,412p' ops/conductor/conductor-start-plan.md; grep -n 'class: expected' docs/wire.md

envelope.note:
REVIEW — Opus 5, exact model id claude-opus-5, read-only. Ref 8d5d256b943232cf7366d3d78c415d6e01609901 against base 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76, measured from the supplied context/diff.patch and the snapshot tree. Verdict: changes.

Scope reviewed. The four-document completion of adoption units 1b/1c: conductor-start-plan.md (trusted launch descriptor, connection/onboarding/resume binding, startup refusal boundary), harness-capabilities.md (compile_launch, safe argv grammar, capability identity encoding), permission-surface.md (normalized tool Request/Decision), probes-lever.md (disposable diagnostic bootstrap, live observation format, acceptance matrix). The diff range also carries the owner assignment at .dev/ladder-inputs/conduct-launcher-owner.md and the producer record .dev/records/dispatches/20260906T103421Z-code-codex-20aa14.json; both are preserved inputs and were not re-litigated under this read profile.

What I checked and what held. All three in/ files were read whole. Every cross-document anchor cited by the added text resolves to a real heading in this snapshot: trusted-conductor-launch-descriptor, safe-argv-grammar, normalized-conductor-tool-interface, conduct-live-diagnostics, lane-policy.md#bootstrap-and-minimum-complete-activation, discovery-lever.md#trusted-configuration-and-bounded-profiles and devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md#capability-evidence-and-freshness. The linked reports and the two harness files exist. The two acceptance claims are accurate against their reports: discovery-contract-acceptance-20260906.md records completed independent review "ready for the next test/implementation stage" and explicitly not activation; worker-launch-contract-acceptance-20260906.md records C1/C2 review completion and retains the adoption dependencies. Replacing "Step 1 ends only after admission for independent test authors" is therefore supported, and the pending lane-boundary enforcement track is not silently closed — it remains stated at conductor-start-plan.md:25-27. The four JSON examples parse by inspection and satisfy their own declared grammars: the selection fragment carries all six keys with ID-valid harness/profile; the adapter-argv manifest obeys name/forms/values/repeatable, flag-without-values and unique-name rules; both admissible vectors match; the Decision refusal carries a lower-case class and nonempty expected/found/needed with found drawn from the fixed Reason set.

Against the aim: the descriptor, Request, Decision and observation report are genuinely closed and each states its key-completeness rule. Safe forwarding is specified to byte level with a catch-all ("any token not consumed by a rule"), reserved classes, and pre-effect rejection without echoing rejected values. Model selection is kept off any job-model table and requires configured and explicit selection to agree, with requested-versus-actual observation. The five selection axes are separate. Resume revalidates custody, policy, selection, config/anchors, adapter, tokens and MCP catalogue before restoring state, and re-verifies the actual client connection. Refusal versus unreachable is drawn correctly in both directions: a token rejected by an available grammar is a deterministic refusal, unknown installed syntax blocks capability admission, and UNREACHABLE is reserved for inability to measure. No new executor, store, registry, writable MCP tool or Symfony/vendor dependency is introduced, and lane-boundary reads (contract/application inspection within custody) stay inspection-only. Daybreak's HAND, ARGV, SECRET and LIVE dispositions survive as acceptance duties in the reviewer's own terms — including the disposable outer canary rather than an arbitrary host target, transient write-restore observation, the corrected UNREACHABLE terminology, and the bounded credential-canary scope — and the text repeatedly states that contract acceptance is not runtime admission. The "not a lever contract" line was correctly updated when the file gained one; "What this is not" is untouched and still true.

Findings. One p2 and seven p3, all interface-precision defects in the frozen text, listed in findings[]. The p2 is that launch_id is typed as discovery's ID, which cannot hold the canonical execution record id form, while the same section leans on that record for model observation and custody with no field binding the two. The p3s: the undefined-and-colliding `Selection` type name; the surviving "Nothing here can Abort" in probes-lever's Exits section beside the new exit 3; the undefined field mapping between descriptor adapter and identity adapter, which leaves the normalizer outside the binding digest; evaluate_tool frozen in permission-surface with no counterpart in lane-policy.md and no note that bucket 1a still owes one; cleanup=unreachable with no declared exit class; the CLI synopsis still not showing where `--` may appear; and a fixed refusal template embedding the wire's own "; " separator. Each is a small edit in the same four files; none reopens accepted discovery, C1/C2 or lane-policy architecture, and none demands code.

Limits, declared. This sandbox refused git, python3 and awk invocations. I therefore could not run git diff --check, verify the commit trailers or authorship of 8d5d256, or machine-parse the JSON examples and the committed record; the examples were validated by reading them against their declared grammars, and file/anchor existence by ls and grep. I did not compare the committed dispatch record byte-for-byte against in/ag-conduct-interface-producer.json — looked at, not measured. No source, test, settings or host write, no network, no vendor launch, no probe or suite run occurred. Nothing here admits a harness, activates policy or publishes a review, handoff or AAR.
